scoring_ownership.business_correctness: internal .75 actual release byte preservation (any placement for independent content credit; layout owned by boundary) + .25 actual selected-part SHA eligibility and top release/version fields
scoring_ownership.boundary_cases: internal .40 original note bytes/path preservation + .40 single-root exact-case fixed paths and all intact-source graph edges + .20 recorded exact/casefold conflict routing. Changed-byte sources own their missing graph edges to avoid cascade; an extra wrapper preserves independent note-byte credit; v2 additionally binds every present original release byte to its required target, so a permutation cannot pass. Missing original byte checks remain owned by business content.
scoring_ownership.delivery_integrity: internal .60 input SHA/member protection + .15 native audit JSON + .10 native handoff summary + .15 six summary facts
scoring_ownership.evidence_binding: internal .40 original member hashes/sizes/nonempty subset of valid source part IDs + .20 original note provenance + .20 actual resource relation identity + .10 input hashes + .10 old-release exclusion identity/reason; v2 binds reported member/note target paths to actual restored SHA. Canonical targets affected by an already-scored artifact mismatch are explicitly not_assessed (neutral), not verified. A fabricated alternate path fails; reporting the actual path of a misplaced wrapper remains valid provenance and layout loses separately.

usability_boundary: Actual authored-reference local browser tests exist outside candidate delivery. Candidate grading is original byte preservation plus independently parsed local dependency/fragment graph; it does not claim candidate app launch, source execution or real Harness behavior. Never execute arbitrary changed candidate script to inspect static restoration.

infrastructure: Missing/drift GT/helper is evaluation exception; candidate missing/corrupt payload, note loss, mixed selected metadata, nested root, wrong case or malformed delivery loses corresponding obligations.
